title: Full backup enables linkage of student records across datasets

title: Backed-up grade and assignment records can serve as attributable evidence
description: Stored grade records, submissions, and related account directory information can be attributed to specific individuals, making it difficult for data subjects to deny association with particular coursework outcomes or records once replicated to the provider.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with named or uniquely referenced students and possibly instructors.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is plausible because attributable records are replicated, but the flow description does not explicitly mention signatures, audit logs, or evidentiary use.

title: Excessive amount of personal data in nightly full backups
description: The flow sends full grade records, assignments, and directory data in nightly backups, indicating a large amount of personal data is processed and disclosed rather than a minimized subset needed for resilience purposes.
assumptions: Assumes incremental or reduced-content backups could meet the operational objective.

title: Backup frequency may exceed functional necessity

title: Data subjects may be unaware that full academic records are replicated to a third-party host
